sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Bates County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Three desks in the Bates County offices in Butler cover most property tax questions, and each has a room on West Dakota Street. The Collector/Treasurer, Kacie Robey, is in Room 2 at 103 West Dakota, Butler, MO 64730. The Assessor, Carl Bettels, is in Room 4, and the County Clerk, Jami Page, is in Room 1. Courthouse offices keep 8:30 am to 4:30 pm hours on weekdays and close from noon to 1 pm.

The Collector answers at 660-679-3341 or through the courthouse line at 660-386-7776, option 3. The Assessor is reached at option 4 on the courthouse line, and the Recorder of Deeds, Danyelle Baker, in Room 3 handles the deed side of a sale. The Collector also acts as county Treasurer, so one office both collects and distributes the money to schools, townships and the health center.

sections.h2: What is Bates County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Bates County is a rural part of west central Missouri, close to the Kansas line and part of the Kansas City metropolitan area. It covers 851 square miles, of which 837 are land, and it was organized in 1841 and named for Frederick Bates, the state's second governor. Butler is the county seat and largest city, and Adrian, Drexel, Rich Hill, Amsterdam, Amoret, Hume and Rockville are among the other towns.

The 2020 census counted 16,042 residents, with an estimate of 16,512 for 2025. All of that population is classed as rural. The county had 7,189 housing units, 11.1% of them vacant, and 74.3% of occupied homes were owner occupied. Interstate 49, US 71 and Routes 18 and 52 are the main roads.

School districts reaching into the county include Butler R-V, Adrian R-III, Rich Hill R-IV, Drexel R-IV, Hume R-VIII, Miami R-I, Ballard R-II and Archie R-V. Which district sits on your parcel affects the levy lines on the bill, so look at the statement itself.

sections.h2: When does a Bates County tax bill turn delinquent?
sections.html:
Missouri law sets the line at the start of the new year. Under RSMo 139.100, once a taxpayer misses the deadline, the collector must add a penalty after the first of January. Mail is treated as paid on its postmark date, and a certified or registered mailing counts on the date of certification. If the postmark is missing or unreadable, the collector uses judgment and documents the call.

For 2026 bills, that makes December 31, 2026 the practical cutoff, with the new penalty arriving on January 1, 2027. The county has a 24-hour drop box on the east side of the Administration Building.

sections.h2: What are the ways to pay in Bates County?
sections.html:
The Collector's website lists payments in person, by mail, online and through the drop box. Card fees are passed to the payer and none of that fee goes to Bates County, which the site ties to RSMo 139.055.

  • In person at Room 2, 103 West Dakota, Butler.
  • By mail to the Collector's office, with a postmark on or before the deadline.
  • Online through the Collector's website, where debit cards cost $4.00 and credit cards cost 2.45%.
  • In the 24-hour drop box on the east side of the Administration Building.

The Collector adds that a paid receipt shown on a phone screen works at the DMV or Department of Revenue office.

sections.h2: How does the Bates County tax sale work?
sections.html:
The Collector holds a delinquent real estate tax certificate sale on the fourth Monday of every August. For the 2026 sale, the eligible properties were published on July 22, 2026, and full payment had to arrive in the office before 4:30 PM on Friday, August 21, 2026 to stop the auction. Both dates have passed, so any 2026 sale outcome is a matter of record at the Collector's office.

Payment on a sale-eligible parcel must be made by cash, money order, card or cashier's check. Web and phone payments were not allowed for those parcels.

If a buyer wins at a tax auction, RSMo 140.405 gives the owner a right to redeem. The buyer must send notice by first class and certified mail at least ninety days before the date they can take the deed, and an owner who wants to sell or add liens must redeem first. Anyone considering a sale of a delinquent parcel should talk to the Collector about the redemption amount first.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Bates County assessment?
sections.html:
The first step is to ask the Assessor's office, Room 4, to review your value. If the answer is unsatisfactory, the next step is the local Board of Equalization. Ask the County Clerk's office in Room 1 when the board meets and how to book a hearing.

After that, Missouri law gives you a right to appeal to the State Tax Commission. RSMo 138.430 sets that window at the deadline stated in the chapter or thirty days after the board's final action, whichever is later. The Commission says the filing is due on or before September 30 of the assessment year or within thirty days of the board's decision, whichever is later, and the board's decision letter must be uploaded with the complaint.

Owners should note a rule for estates: property held by an LLC, trust, association or estate must be represented by an attorney at the Commission, while a home owned by a person or persons need not be. The Commission's phone number is 573-751-1715.

sections.h2: What if I disagree with a bill and still need to pay?
sections.html:
Missouri allows payment under protest. Under RSMo 139.031, you pay the full bill before the delinquency date and file a written statement with the Collector listing your grounds and the value you claim. The Collector sends the undisputed share to the taxing districts and holds the disputed share in a separate fund.

A taxpayer who protests must start a circuit court action against the Collector within ninety days of filing the protest, unless a timely assessment appeal is already pending. That pending appeal, filed with the State Tax Commission or the court, takes the place of a separate suit.

Refunds of erroneous tax are also possible. A written application must be filed within three years of the payment.

sections.h2: What should a Bates County seller do about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Ask for a payoff figure from the Collector's office before the contract date, and check the Collector's records for earlier years. Then give that number to the title company.

  • Confirm all current and delinquent real estate bills on the parcel.
  • Find out whether the parcel appears on a tax sale list.
  • Ask the Assessor about any pending change of value.
  • Confirm the Recorder in Room 3 will record the deed and release of any old deed of trust.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property taxes in Bates County, Missouri?
faqs.a: Pay the Bates County Collector in Room 2 at 103 West Dakota, Butler, by mail, online, or in the east side drop box of the Administration Building. Phone 660-679-3341. Card payments carry a fee passed to the payer.

faqs.q: When does a Bates County property tax bill become delinquent?
faqs.a: After December 31. Missouri law adds a penalty after January 1, and mailed payments count on their postmark date. Mail well before the cutoff so the postmark falls inside the window.

faqs.q: When is the Bates County tax sale?
faqs.a: The fourth Monday of August every year. For 2026, owners had to pay in full in the office by 4:30 PM on Friday, August 21, 2026 to prevent the auction, so that date has passed.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Bates County property value?
faqs.a: Start with the Assessor in Room 4, then use the Board of Equalization through the County Clerk. A further appeal goes to the Missouri State Tax Commission by September 30 or thirty days after the board's decision, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Can I pay my taxes under protest in Bates County?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the whole bill before it turns delinquent and give the Collector a written statement of your grounds. A court action to recover the protested amount must follow within ninety days unless an assessment appeal is already pending.
